newsitem.title: USA: Late U.S. West Coast prods sag with lower NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: Late U.S. West Coast prods sag with lower NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices slipped with a lower NYMEX products and crude market Friday, amid thin discussion and no reported deals, brokers said.
April NYMEX crude settled 30 cents lower at $21.39 a barrel, while March gasoline dropped 0.96 cents a gallon to 61.82 cents a gallon.
"That's what's bringing us down" said one broker, referring to the weaker NYMEX market.
CARB gasoline in Los Angeles fell a half cent to 72.50/73.50 cents a gallon Friday.
Bay grades fell 1.25 cents a gallon to 69.75 cents.
L.A. CARB diesel was notionally about three cents lower at 74/74.50 cents, while low sulphur diesel dropped two cents to 68/69 cents.
